source_basis: Paper models passing interactions as undirected weighted graph (adjacency matrix). Direction of pass is discarded.
interpretation: Undirected assumption simplifies computation but loses tactical asymmetry (who initiates vs receives). For D-type problems, this tradeoff of simplicity vs information loss is common.
applicability: Any network-based teamwork/interaction model faces this directed-vs-undirected choice. Pattern: state the simplification explicitly as an assumption.
counterevidence: Directed passing networks in sports analytics literature (e.g., Pena & Touchette 2012) show direction matters for identifying playmakers.

source_basis: K-means applied to adjacency vectors to find player clusters. K chosen manually without elbow method or silhouette analysis.
interpretation: Manual K selection is a weakness but common in contest papers under time pressure. The lack of systematic K selection undermines reproducibility.
applicability: Any clustering application should document K selection rationale. Pattern: mention why K was chosen even if heuristic.
counterevidence: Elbow method, gap statistic, or silhouette scores provide principled K selection.

source_basis: Adversarial regression: team score S minus opponent score S_opp must match game result. Greedy exhaustive weight search over 5 indicators.
interpretation: Adversarial framing is creative — most student papers score teams independently. Exhaustive search avoids local optima but discretization loses precision. No cross-validation reported.
applicability: Any head-to-head competition model benefits from adversarial framing. Pattern: define score as relative, not absolute.
counterevidence: Cross-validation and continuous optimization (gradient descent) would strengthen the approach.

source_basis: Generalization model maps soccer indicators to abstract teamwork via analogy. Leadership Intensity and Effective Coordination introduced as composite formulas.
interpretation: Ambitious scope extension typical of D-type papers. Formulas are proposed without data, making them aspirational rather than validated. Authors themselves note low persuasibility.
applicability: Cross-domain analogies show modeling ambition but need at minimum a toy validation case.
counterevidence: No empirical validation provided; authors acknowledge limitation.

source_basis: Four assumptions listed: undirected graph, substitution stability, opponent equality, player homogeneity.
interpretation: Assumptions are stated clearly (good practice) but are strong simplifications. Player homogeneity especially unrealistic. Assumptions section is concise (4 bullets) which is typical for Outstanding-level D papers.
applicability: Clear assumption listing is a transferable practice. Pattern: bullet-list assumptions before model.
counterevidence: Player heterogeneity is fundamental to sports analytics; homogeneity assumption is knowingly unrealistic.

source_basis: 'Each player, either of Huskies or of opponents, has the same physical quality and individual ability' — homogeneity assumption.
interpretation: This assumption enables the model to isolate teamwork from individual talent. It is a deliberate simplification that strengthens the paper's focus but weakens predictive validity.
applicability: Pattern: when modeling interaction quality, explicitly assume away individual variation to sharpen the teamwork signal.
counterevidence: Real performance depends heavily on individual player quality.

source_basis: Data source: passing events from match records. Adjacency matrix constructed from passer-receiver pairs.
interpretation: Event-level data (pass-by-pass) is granular enough for network construction. Paper does not discuss data quality issues (missed passes, recording errors).
applicability: Pattern: when using event data, acknowledge recording fidelity.
counterevidence: No data quality assessment reported.

source_basis: Training on Huskies' season data: 'there are 20 groups of weight coefficient combinations that meet the conditions.'
interpretation: 20 feasible solutions from exhaustive search is a surprisingly small number, suggesting tight constraints or coarse discretization. Paper selects LowestError from these 20.
applicability: Pattern: report solution count from enumeration to calibrate how constrained the problem is.
counterevidence: With finer discretization, more solutions would likely appear.

source_basis: 'Nowadays teamwork is playing an increasingly important role in all walks of life' — classic L2 opener with 随着 calque.
interpretation: This opening formula (Nowadays + increasingly important + broad scope) is extremely common in Chinese-authored MCM papers. AI models almost never generate this pattern, making it a strong human-writing signal.
applicability: High-value reusable pattern for D-type abstract openings. Store as language unit.
counterevidence: Native English academic writers rarely use 'Nowadays' as a paper opener.

source_basis: 'With the development of social interconnections, the challenge people faced has become complex increasingly.' — 随着...的发展 calque + postposed adverb.
interpretation: Double L2 signal: (1) With-the-development-of opener is direct translation of 随着...的发展, (2) 'complex increasingly' has postposed adverb (Chinese word order). AI models would write 'increasingly complex.'
applicability: Store both patterns. The postposed-adverb error is especially valuable as an authenticity marker.
counterevidence: Correct English: 'increasingly complex' not 'complex increasingly.'

source_basis: 'In a gesture to explore other structured indicators' — gesture misused for effort/attempt (L2 error).
interpretation: 'In a gesture to' appears twice in the paper (pages 9 and 19). Author likely intended 'In an effort to' or 'In a bid to'. This is a distinctive L2 error that AI would never produce.
applicability: Extremely valuable authenticity marker. Store as language unit. AI correction systems would fix this, so its presence signals genuine human writing.
counterevidence: Correct English: 'In an effort to' or 'In a bid to.'

source_basis: 'The selection of the network parameters of the passing network is scientific and reasonable.' — 科学合理 calque.
interpretation: 'Scientific and reasonable' (科学合理) is a fixed Chinese academic phrase. Used verbatim in self-praise context, which is culturally appropriate in Chinese academic writing but unusual in English.
applicability: Store as language unit and strengths-section pattern. AI models avoid this self-praise formula.
counterevidence: English academic convention avoids explicit self-praise as 'scientific and reasonable.'

source_basis: 'resulting in a low persuasibility of the model' — coined word 'persuasibility' (should be persuasiveness/persuasion).
interpretation: Author coined 'persuasibility' by analogy with other -ibility words. This creative error is extremely unlikely from AI (which knows the correct form) and is a strong human-writing signal.
applicability: Store as language unit. Coined words from morphological over-generalization are powerful authenticity markers.
counterevidence: Correct form: persuasiveness or persuasive power.

source_basis: 'it can also measure the overall emotion between teammates' — emotion used for cohesion/chemistry.
interpretation: 'Emotion' here likely translates 感情 which means both emotion and interpersonal bond/chemistry. This semantic transfer error is characteristic of L2 Chinese-English writing.
applicability: Store as language unit. Semantic field confusion (emotion/bond/chemistry) is a human L2 pattern.
counterevidence: English would use 'cohesion', 'chemistry', or 'rapport.'

source_basis: 'accords with the actual situation' — 符合实际情况 calque.
interpretation: Direct translation of 符合实际情况, a very common Chinese academic justification phrase. AI models use 'aligns with real-world conditions' or 'matches observed behavior.'
applicability: Store as language unit. This calque is one of the most reliable Chinese-to-English transfer markers.
counterevidence: English equivalent: 'consistent with observed data' or 'matches real-world conditions.'

source_basis: 'The purpose of this paper is to create a model' — purpose-of-this-paper template.
interpretation: Standard MCM objective-statement formula. Used more in Chinese-authored papers than native English academic writing (which prefers 'We propose' or 'This study develops').
applicability: Store as language unit for objective statements in abstracts.
counterevidence: Native English preference: 'We propose/develop' rather than 'The purpose of this paper is.'

source_basis: 'It's of great significance to clarify whether strategies are universally effective' — 具有重要意义 calque.
interpretation: 'Of great significance' (具有重要意义) is another fixed Chinese academic phrase. AI models typically use 'It is important to determine' or 'A key question is whether.'
applicability: Store as language unit for discussion-section significance claims.
counterevidence: English preference: 'It is important' or 'A key question is.'

source_basis: Adversarial regression constrains score difference to match game outcome. Greedy search finds 20 feasible weight sets; LowestError selected.
interpretation: Logic is sound but the constraint is self-referential: the model is defined to fit the training data. No holdout or cross-validation prevents overfitting.
applicability: Pattern: when using exhaustive search with outcome constraints, always report out-of-sample validation.
counterevidence: Overfitting risk high with small sample and exhaustive fit to training outcomes.

source_basis: 'Only by adjusting the strategy based on the opponents' strategy... can the Huskies more likely to win' — key adversarial conclusion.
interpretation: Central conclusion is logically supported by the adversarial regression framework. The argument structure (model → insight → recommendation) is clear and well-organized.
applicability: Pattern: state the key insight as a conditional — 'only by X can Y' — to emphasize the adversarial nature of competition.
counterevidence: Conclusion may overstate certainty given the model's limitations.

source_basis: Regression equation: S = 0.1·Coordination + 0.3·Distribution + 0.15·Tempo + 0.25·Flexibility + 0.2·Pressing (approximate weights).
interpretation: Distribution has highest weight (0.3), consistent with the paper's conclusion that contribution uniformity matters most. Weight ordering is interpretable.
applicability: Pattern: report weight ordering and interpret the most influential indicator.
counterevidence: Weights depend on indicator scaling; no normalization procedure described.

source_basis: 5-3-2 formation recommended for Huskies based on formation-performance comparison table.
interpretation: Practical recommendation derived from model output. Formation comparison adds tactical value beyond pure statistics.
applicability: Pattern: translate model output into actionable domain-specific recommendation.
counterevidence: Formation recommendation based on limited sample (one season).

source_basis: Italy National Team used as external benchmark. Huskies compared against Italy's passing patterns.
interpretation: External benchmark adds credibility by comparing against known successful team. However, comparing college team to national team has questionable validity.
applicability: Pattern: use external benchmark for model validation, but acknowledge level differences.
counterevidence: College vs national team comparison has obvious confounders.

source_basis: Sensitivity analysis varies error limit ε from 0 to 2. Weight stability examined as ε changes.
interpretation: Standard sensitivity approach: vary key parameter and observe output stability. ε variation is the right parameter to test since it controls the adversarial constraint.
applicability: Pattern: identify the parameter most critical to model validity and vary it.
counterevidence: Only one parameter varied; joint sensitivity not explored.

source_basis: Tempo sensitivity: 30-pass, 50-pass, and 70-pass windows compared. 30-pass too jagged, 70-pass too smooth, 50-pass goldilocks.
interpretation: Goldilocks argument (too rough / too smooth / just right) is an effective and intuitive validation technique. However, 'just right' is subjective without a formal criterion.
applicability: Pattern: test multiple window sizes and use the goldilocks argument to justify selection.
counterevidence: No formal criterion for 'just right' — purely visual assessment.

source_basis: Paper structure: Abstract → Introduction → Assumptions/Notation → Network Model → Evaluation Model → Strategy Discussion → Generalization → Sensitivity → Strengths/Weaknesses → References → Appendix (code).
interpretation: Standard D-type structure with emphasis on model building (network + evaluation). Generalization section (unusual) shows ambition. Code appendix is good practice.
applicability: Pattern: D-type papers benefit from explicit generalization section to show broader applicability.
counterevidence: None identified

source_basis: Abstract uses task-labeled structure: 'In TASK 1... In TASK 2...' to organize method preview.
interpretation: Task-labeling in abstract mirrors the MCM problem structure (Task 1, 2, 3). This explicit mapping shows the reader exactly which tasks are addressed.
applicability: Pattern: mirror competition task labels in abstract structure when problem has numbered sub-tasks.
counterevidence: None identified

source_basis: Self-assessment: lists 2 strengths (parameter selection, adversarial evaluation) and 2 weaknesses (insufficient individual analysis, unquantifiable generalization).
interpretation: Honest self-assessment. Weaknesses genuinely identify real limitations rather than being disguised strengths. This candor is characteristic of genuine student writing.
applicability: Pattern: strengths/weaknesses section should identify real limitations, not disguised strengths.
counterevidence: None identified

source_basis: 'Last but not least, we generalize our model to more teamwork and indicate how to build an effective team' — cliche + scope escalation.
interpretation: 'Last but not least' is a cliche that AI models have been trained to avoid but human L2 writers still use frequently. Combined with grandiose scope claim ('build an effective team'), this is a strong human-writing signal.
applicability: Store as language unit. Cliches that AI avoids are valuable authenticity markers.
counterevidence: Native English academic writing avoids 'last but not least.'

source_basis: 'According to the training of the Greedy Algorithm, there are 20 groups of weight coefficient combinations that meet the conditions.' — 满足条件 calque.
interpretation: 'Meet the conditions' (满足条件) is a direct Chinese calque. AI models would write 'satisfy the constraints' or 'pass the validation criteria.'
applicability: Store as language unit for results sections reporting algorithm outputs.
counterevidence: English preference: 'satisfy the constraints' or 'meet the criteria.'

source_basis: 'we can have a general idea about the importance between the five indicators' — casual register in results.
interpretation: 'Have a general idea about' is colloquial/casual register, inappropriate for formal academic writing. AI models maintain formal register. This casualness signals authentic student writing.
applicability: Pattern: casual register in analysis sections is a human-writing marker.
counterevidence: Formal English: 'we can assess the relative importance of' or 'we can infer the significance of.'

source_basis: 'This shows that the player is involved in the attacking development of his team.' — this-shows-that connector.
interpretation: 'This shows that' is an extremely common Chinese academic English connector (这说明). Used for interpreting results. AI models prefer 'This indicates' or 'This suggests.'
applicability: Store as language unit for interpretation connectors.
counterevidence: English academic preference: 'This indicates/suggests/implies.'

source_basis: 'In order to further understand the network model, we should select some relevant indicators.' — in-order-to + should modality.
interpretation: 'In order to further' + 'we should select' combines purpose clause with should-modality. Both are more common in Chinese-authored English than native English academic writing.
applicability: Store as language unit for method-transition sentences.
counterevidence: Native English preference: 'To better characterize' + 'we identify/select' (no 'should').

source_basis: 'the network for the ball passing can be described as an adjacency matrix in Data Structure' — field reference as proper noun.
interpretation: Capitalizing 'Data Structure' as if it were a course title (数据结构 is a standard CS course in Chinese universities). AI models would write 'in data structure theory' or 'as a graph-theoretic construct.'
applicability: Pattern: field/course references as proper nouns signal Chinese academic background.
counterevidence: English convention: lowercase 'data structures' unless referring to a specific course.

source_basis: Five indicators defined: Coordination (avg clustering coeff), Distribution (degree std dev), Tempo (50-pass time), Flexibility (y-std), Pressing (x-mean).
interpretation: Creative indicator selection mapping network metrics to tactical concepts. Each indicator has a clear intuitive meaning. The Static/Dynamic taxonomy adds organizational clarity.
applicability: Pattern: map abstract metrics to domain-interpretable names to increase readability.
counterevidence: Some indicators (e.g., Pressing as x-mean) are oversimplified proxies.

source_basis: Weight values remain stable as ε varies in [0.5, 1.5], diverge outside this range.
interpretation: Stability plateau in middle range supports model robustness claim. Divergence at extremes is expected and honest reporting.
applicability: Pattern: report stability range and note where parameters diverge.
counterevidence: Only one parameter tested; multivariate sensitivity missing.
